newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-HUNDREDS ATTEND FASSI SERVICE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-HUNDREDS ATTEND FASSI SERVICE.

text.p: The figure skating community turned out en masse for a memorial service to the late coach Carlo Fassi at the Olympic Museum on Sunday.

Hundreds of people including past and present champions, coaches and officials along with International Olympic Committee president Juan Antonio Samaranch attended the service for the U.S.-based Italian.
Fassi died of a heart attack on Thursday aged 67.

In a brief address, Samaranch, whose IOC headquarters are in Lausanne, called Fassi "a great man of sport" and presented the Olympic flag to Fassi's wife Christa, who was there with their three children.
International Skating Union (ISU) president Ottavio Cinquanta and other ISU officials also attended.
The service was presided over by American Dick Button, the Olympic champion in 1948 and 1952 and a five-times world champion who was a close friend of Fassi, the European champion in 1953 and 1954.
Nicole Bobek, Fassi's main pupil at the world championships, who placed 13th, and new champion Tara Lipinski also attended.
